title: Uncurried maps from a finite presentation lift into a stage tensor module
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed partially ordered set, $F:I\to\mathrm{CRing}$ a functor, $A=\operatorname{colim}_I F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], $i\in I$, and $M,N$ be $F_i$-modules in a common universe containing the ring universe. Assume $M$ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Given an $F_i$-linear map $h:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{F_i}^{A}(A\otimes_{F_i}N)$, there exist $j\ge i$ and an $F_i$-linear map $a:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{F_i}^{F_j}(F_j\otimes_{F_i}N)$. For every $A$-linear isomorphism $e:A\otimes_{F_i}N\to A\otimes_{F_j}(F_j\otimes_{F_i}N)$ which sends $1\otimes n$ to $1\otimes(1\otimes n)$, one has $e(h(x))=1\otimes a(x)$ for every $x\in M$. There is no finite-presentation assumption on $N$.

proof.text: Restrict the diagram to the nonempty directed upper tail of i. Regard each Fj tensor over Fi with N as an Fi-module. Tensor the Fi-algebra transition maps and coprojections with N; functoriality and cocone naturality give the directed-system and compatibility laws. The representation and eventual-zero clauses of directedColimitBaseChangeElementwise apply to this system.

Use Module.FinitePresentation.exists_fin to write M as a finite free module modulo a finitely generated submodule K. Represent the images of its finitely many basis vectors at stages, move them to a common upper bound, and extend by the basis universal property to a linear map a0. Equality with h after coprojection holds on the basis, hence everywhere. Each generator of K maps to zero in the final tensor module. The eventual-zero clause gives a later vanishing stage for each generator. Choose a common upper bound, transport a0 there, and use the directed-system law to kill every generator of K. The span criterion then kills K. Descend with Submodule.liftQ and compose with the presentation equivalence. This also handles empty bases and relation sets.

Convert the natural Fi-actions on the tensor modules to the displayed restriction-of-scalars actions using algebraMap_smul. For any comparison e satisfying the unit-tensor equation, tensor induction shows e sends the coprojection image of each stage tensor t to 1 tensor t: on a pure tensor use A-linearity, the unit-tensor equation, and tensor balancing; zero and addition are immediate. Apply this identity to the descended linear map and its coprojection equation.

theorem exists_stage_restricted_hom
    {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat) (i : I) (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v} (F.obj i))
    [Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i) M]
    (h : M ⟶ (restrictScalars (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.ι F i))).obj
      ((extendScalars (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.ι F i))).obj N)) :
    ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j),
      let rij := CommRingCat.Hom.hom (F.map (homOfLE hij))
      let rj := CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.ι F j)
      let ri := CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.ι F i)
      ∃ (a : M ⟶ (restrictScalars rij).obj ((extendScalars rij).obj N)),
        ∀ (e : (extendScalars ri).obj N ≅
          (extendScalars rj).obj ((extendScalars rij).obj N)),
          (∀ n : N, e.hom ((1 : ↑(colimit F : CommRingCat)) ⊗ₜ[F.obj i, ri] n) =
            (1 : ↑(colimit F : CommRingCat)) ⊗ₜ[F.obj j, rj]
              ((1 : ↑(F.obj j)) ⊗ₜ[F.obj i, rij] n)) →
          ∀ m : M, e.hom (h m) =
            (1 : ↑(colimit F : CommRingCat)) ⊗ₜ[F.obj j, rj] (a m)
